result:
This is decisive. The **only** applicable axiom for proving `AE.intersectsLine DB` is `lines_intersect` (Euclid's fifth-postulate converse), and it **requires `e0.sameSide d AB`** as a hypothesis. That same-side fact is exactly what `proposition_23` fails to provide: its conclusion is only `∃f, f ≠ a ∧ ∠f:a:b = ∠a:b:d`, with `f`'s side of `AB` unconstrained.

I have a rigorous Euclidean countermodel: with `A=(0,1), C=(0,-1), B=(-½,0)` (so `hgt` holds since the chord is short) and `e0=(-1,1)`, we get `∠e0:a:b = ∠a:b:d` (equal, as required) yet line `AE` is `y=1`, parallel to line `DB` (the x-axis) — **no intersection**. Every hypothesis holds; `hint1` is false. So `hint1` is not entailed. Euclid's I.23 pins the construction side off the figure; the formalized `proposition_23` drops it. This is a genuine Euclid/figure gap, not something I can derive or an axiom I may add.

GAP_FLAG: Book3/Prop25 hint1 (AE.intersectsLine DB — existence of the meet E of ray AE and perpendicular DB, construction for sentences 3.25.6–3.25.7; same gap recurs at hint3/step21 in case 3) :: proposition_23 yields e0 with ∠e0:a:b=∠a:b:d on an UNCONSTRAINED side of AB, but AE∩DB requires e0.sameSide d AB (demanded by the sole applicable axiom lines_intersect, the 5th-postulate converse); the opposite-side witness gives equal ALTERNATE angles ⟹ AE∥DB — a valid Euclidean countermodel (A=(0,1),C=(0,-1),B=(-½,0),e0=(-1,1)) satisfying every hypothesis with no intersection — so hint1 is not entailed (Euclid's I.23 fixes the side by construction; the formalized proposition_23 drops it).

import SystemE
import Book1.Prop11.Main
import Book1.Prop08.Main
set_option linter.unusedVariables false
set_option linter.unnecessarySeqFocus false

namespace Elements.Book3
open Elements.Book1

set_option systemE.solverTime 30 in
theorem helper_3_25_step2 (a b c d : Point) (AC DB : Line)
    (hAa : a.onLine AC) (hAc : c.onLine AC) (hac : a ≠ c) (hbAC : ¬b.onLine AC)
    (hab_cb : |(a─b)| = |(c─b)|) (hadc : between a d c) (hstep1 : |(a─d)| = |(d─c)|)
    (hdDB : d.onLine DB) (hbDB : b.onLine DB) : ∠ a:d:b = ∟ := by
  -- Honor the [Prop.~1.11] citation: a perpendicular exists at d on AC.
  euclid_apply (proposition_11 a c d AC) as f
  -- SSS: triangles ADB and CDB are congruent, so ∠ADB = ∠CDB.
  euclid_apply (line_from_points a b) as AB
  euclid_apply (line_from_points c b) as CB
  euclid_apply (proposition_8 d a b d c b AC AB DB AC CB DB)
  -- Two equal adjacent angles on the straight line AC ⟹ right angle.
  euclid_apply (perpendicular_if a c d b AC)
  euclid_finish

end Elements.Book3
